The predicted sulfur TES cost was compared against the quotes received from fabricators such as PCL construction services located in Bakersfield, California in Figure 19. PCL provided the quote for 23-ton sulfur TES system with 2” internal heat exchanger piping configuration that was fabricated. The cost breakdown between the vessel and internal heat exchanger was also provided. The difference between the predicted cost and quote is within 8%. Another fabricator provided the quote for 250-ton sulfur TES system with 1-inch internal heat exchanger piping circuit. The average difference is within 8%. It is noted that the pilot-scale 23-ton sulfur TES costs ~170 $/kWh and the 250-ton Page 40 of 87 DE-EE0009329 Element 16 Technologies, Inc. sulfur TES costs 60 $/kWh, which is evidence of the reduction in storage cost per unit capacity with economies of scale. The model satisfactorily captures the relationship between sulfur TES cost and storage capacity size. Overall, the cost model prediction is within ± 10% of the cost estimates from fabrication partners. Figure 19: Comparison of cost predicted by model versus quote received from fabricator Site Integration Installation Review Element 16 was unable to secure a signed agreement with a host site for pilot prototype testing (GNG-2F). The original solar thermal partner indicated that their solar field outlet heat transfer fluid temperature (< 200 oC) would not satisfy the project goals. Element 16 engaged in talks with other potential site partners, but they were unable to commit due to scheduling uncertainties. In addition, steel prices had increased significantly since the project initiation, requiring renegotiation of pilot performance metrics due to address potential budget constraints. In response, Element 16 proposed modifying the pilot scope to complete the testing activities in-house using simulated solar thermal profiles, while still meeting the originally negotiated performance metrics in the SOPO. The revised plan was reviewed and approved by DOE. During this period, Element 16 also gained valuable insight into the various challenges and best practice for integration of sulfur TES with solar thermal field and process heat application through interactions with engineering and operations team of a petroleum refinery customer.
